Resolves #21622

🌿 *That the Gantt draws links in four types while no example shows a planner making one can no longer be said.*

`examples/gantt/dependencies` is a product launch a planner links by drag: fourteen tasks in three phases, eight links in all four types to begin with, six tasks still unlinked. A drag from a task's finish dot to another task adds a finish-to-start link; a drop on the task itself, or on one that would close a cycle, is refused. A legend draws the four types in the chart's own link colour, the status line names each link a visitor adds, and Reset restores the plan. The engine is untouched; the drive's findings are on the ticket ([drive](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21622#issuecomment-7057091665)).

Evidence: L3 (the example live in headless Chromium at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844, dark and light) → L3 required (AC-6, AC-7). No residuals.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `Dependencies.spec.mjs` › the plan opens with eight links in all four types, a legend of the four, and six tasks unlinked |
| AC-2 | Each bar has one handle, a dot on its finish edge; a drop on another task adds finish to start (`Neo.gantt.Container#linkTasks` → `DependencyStore#addFinishToStart`). The other three types cannot be drawn, so they come with the plan's data. The example's hint says where to drag, and `Dependencies.spec.mjs` › a drag from a finish dot … asserts the new link's endpoints and type. |
| AC-3 | `Dependencies.spec.mjs` › a drop on the same task or on a predecessor is refused: the line turns dashed, the task gets no target ring, no link is added. Frames 6 below, both themes. |
| AC-4 | No gesture or key removes a link. A keyboard user presses L on one task and L on the other (`Dependencies.spec.mjs` › a keyboard user links two tasks with L on each). The chart announces the arming but not the outcome (defect-note 366e444f), so the example's status line names each added link. |
| AC-5 | `test/playwright/e2e/gantt/Dependencies.spec.mjs`: the created link (each arrow carries its record's endpoints and type) and the refused cycle |
| AC-6 | The e2e fixture fails a test on any page or worker error. `Dependencies.spec.mjs` opens the example in each of the five themes `gantt/basic`'s `neo-config.json` lists, at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844, and checks that the legend takes the links' colour. |
| AC-7 | Frames below; cold read in *Cold look* |
| AC-8 | The diff adds only `examples/gantt/dependencies/`, its CSS and its spec |

## Deltas from ticket

- Drag creates finish to start only, the engine's one handle; the four types come with the data and the legend.
- A new link moves nothing by itself; the predecessor's next move cascades it (defect-note 1cbf2f5f). The spec asserts both halves.
- Rows and dates are laid out so each link joins neighbouring rows or runs through empty days; the store review and the page checks before launch are lags of one and two days.
- Task titles are short enough that the task column truncates none at 1440 or 390.
- Reset replaces the records: a link added by drag leaves the store's `data` config as it was, so assigning the seed again would be no change.
- The spec reads the page alone, without the Neural Link, so it needs no entry in the shared e2e selection file (AC-8).

Frame critique: (1) at 1440 the one-day bars cut their titles to `Laun…` and `Retro…`: kept, a 60 px day holds no longer word and the task column names both. (2) The start-to-finish link enters Keep the beta open's end from inside the bar, pointing right: the engine routes that type like finish to start (defect-note 4400f6ed), kept. (3) The two links into Launch day cross the Launch phase's own bar: kept, a phase bar spans every task under it. (4) At 390 the axis shows 2–13 Nov and scrolls for the rest, so Launch day's links leave the frame: kept, the phone frame carries the hint, the legend and the first links. (5) Over a refused task the line looks as it does over an empty row (frames 4 and 6): the engine's look (defect-note b461086f), kept.

## Cold look

One cold reader of my seat's family (Claude Sonnet, a fresh read-only subagent given only the images) read the first version: this example and `gantt/basic` at both sizes, and the state close-ups. What it found, and what became of it:

- **Tangled links** in the right third: lines through Teaser campaign, Marketing and Train support, a line hugging Release notes and Translate the app, three links on one trunk out of Freeze features. Fixed: the plan's rows and dates were re-laid (*Deltas*); the frames above are the new layout.
- **The gesture said neither what it makes nor what follows.** Fixed: the hint now reads "Drag the dot at a task's end onto another task to link them: the second waits for the first to finish."
- **The legend's icons read as tiny and unexplained, and the chart seemed to use two kinds.** Fixed: the row is labelled "Link types", its glyphs are a quarter larger, and the video and landing page now show start to start and finish to finish side by side.
- **At 390 the task column took half the width and the Launch phase showed no bars.** Partly fixed: a day is 18 px instead of 24, so the axis shows 2–13 Nov; the column keeps full titles and the rest scrolls.
- **A refusal looks like a drag that has not reached a task.** The engine's look: defect-note b461086f.
- **An arrow it could not classify inside a bar's end:** the start-to-finish route, defect-note 4400f6ed.

Its comparison: `gantt/basic` looks more finished at 1440 (two short links), this example at 390 (`basic`'s toolbar clips there).

**The graded pair (Round 2).** Two more readers without context (Claude Sonnet, fresh read-only subagents given only the four whole-page frames, unlabelled as "page 1" and "page 2") graded this example and `gantt/basic` at both widths, in swapped order:

| Reader | Shown first | `gantt/basic` | This example | The biggest defect it named here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `gantt/basic` | 4 | 7 | links converge on Launch day and cross its clipped label; the loop into the end of Keep the beta open |
| 2 | this example | 4 | 8 | links converge on a one-day bar whose label reads "Laun…" |

Both would show this example to a colleague. The defect both name is the engine's, not this layout's: the start-to-finish route enters the successor's end (defect-note 4400f6ed), and a one-day bar clips its label inside the bar with no placement beside it (defect-note 0ca50ad2). Moving the start-to-finish link off Launch day would drop the plan's natural case for it, and shorter task names would only hide the second gap, so this round changes no layout.
